sources.title: Hakainde Hichilema: birth, 1986 degree, MBA and Zambia corporate appointments
sources.findings: Read Invest Africa’s 2024 conference biography. It gives 4 June 1962 in Monze, a government bursary, a 1986 University of Zambia BA in economics/business administration and a later Birmingham MBA in finance/business strategy. It dates Coopers & Lybrand leadership to 1994–1998 and Grant Thornton to 1998–2006. The MBA year is not supplied, so do not insert a remembered or inferred year. Promotional wealth, cattle-ranch ranking and shareholding claims were not adopted as current independently audited facts. Its local business context is corroborated explicitly by IGC; these were not global network CEO appointments.

sources.title: President Hichilema: education, local business leadership and economic-policy agenda
sources.findings: Read the IGC profile. It explicitly identifies Coopers Lybrand Zambia in 1994 and Grant Thornton Zambia in 1998, and corroborates the degree subjects, farming/business background and education/economic agenda. It does not independently establish present investment values or global corporate leadership. Its assertion that 2021 had the highest turnout ever conflicts with CRS’s narrower highest-since-2006 description; omit the superlative. Present-tense praise for human rights and governance is not an independent evaluation of the later 2026 controversies.

sources.title: 21 December 2021: Zambia elections, 2006 UPND succession and new government
sources.findings: Read relevant sections of CRS report IF12005, dated 21 December 2021, in the EveryCRSReport archive. It confirms selection as UPND leader and presidential nominee after Anderson Mazoka’s death in 2006, five unsuccessful campaigns before 2021, and the transition from Edgar Lungu. This is a US congressional research publication preserved by an archive, not a Zambian election certificate. Its 2021 parliamentary counts, economic indicators and civil-liberties assessment are historical and not current 2026 statistics. Lungu’s earlier constitutional eligibility disputes are not automatically rulings about Hichilema’s future eligibility.

sources.title: August 2017 update: Hichilema and co-accused released following withdrawal of charges
sources.findings: Read Amnesty’s closed August 2017 action update. It identifies release on 16 August following withdrawal of charges, distinguishing earlier acquittal on an insulting-language count from the later termination of treason proceedings. Its precise arrest date is 10 April, whereas other summaries use 11 April; use April only. The dossier does not describe a treason acquittal after trial, pardon, completed sentence or a legal bar to any future charge. The organisation’s account of video evidence was not substituted for an actual video review; the full case file was not examined.

sources.title: 16 August 2017: prosecutor terminates treason proceedings and judge orders release
sources.findings: Read the short contemporaneous Reuters dispatch syndicated by Investing.com, including the 16 August 2017 timestamp and the judge’s explanation that the director of public prosecutions terminated the proceedings and Hichilema was discharged. This independently corroborates the release, not a determination of the underlying allegations. Live financial-market tickers, current navigation stories and publication-site comments are unrelated and not evidence about the 2017 event. No complete court judgment or criminal docket was reviewed.

sources.title: 24 August 2021: inauguration after sixth presidential campaign
sources.findings: Read AP’s 24 August 2021 inauguration report syndicated by ABC17. It confirms the completed oath following the 12 August election, victory over Lungu and the sixth presidential run after taking party leadership in 2006. The Harare dateline is the report’s filing location, not the inauguration location; the official speech establishes Lusaka’s National Heroes Stadium. Rounded vote totals are not used as exact certified results. Promises of prosperity and unity are reported commitments, not proven delivery.

sources.title: Zambia education-financing profile: January 2022 fee reform and compensatory school grants
sources.findings: Read the relevant UNESCO GEM education-financing profile section. It dates the new fee-removal policy to January 2022, covering pre-primary, primary and secondary levels, with compensatory school grants. This does not establish that every household educational expense, university fee or private-school charge disappeared. The parliamentary brief provides the historical context of earlier free-education policies, so 2022 is an expansion rather than the first ever free schooling in Zambia. The linked archived circular and all project documentation were not separately audited.

sources.title: July 2025 brief on the 2020–2024 free-education audit: expansion, staffing, infrastructure and data limitations
sources.findings: Read the Parliamentary Budget Office’s July 2025 brief introduction, reform history, enrolment discussion and staffing/data/infrastructure findings. It reviews a 2020–2024 performance audit and distinguishes earlier 1965 and 2002 policies from the 2022 expansion. It reports problems with classroom capacity, teacher deployment and discrepancies between administrative data and site visits. Sampled extreme pupil-teacher ratios must not be presented as national averages; forecast and actual recruitment columns differ. A 2025 report date is not the policy start date or proof of the exact state of every school in November 2026. The complete underlying Auditor-General report and individual school records were not examined.

sources.title: 26 June 2024 review: 11 June bond-exchange settlement, remaining creditors and drought constraints
sources.findings: Read the relevant IMF 26 June 2024 review sections on creditor engagement, the bond exchange and drought. It separates a 25 March agreement, 13 May consent solicitation and 11 June settlement. Other commercial creditors and bilateral implementation remained in progress at that time; the bond exchange is not the cancellation of all debt or completion of all restructuring. ECF financing approval/augmentation is a different transaction from restructuring existing bonds. The severe drought’s agricultural and power-generation effects were then-current constraints, while growth figures labelled projections were not adopted as later realised outcomes.

sources.title: 1 September 2026: second inauguration, disputed election and opposition arrests
sources.findings: Read the body of AP’s 1 September 2026 second-inauguration report. It confirms the Lusaka oath, 18 August winner declaration, opposition objections, detentions and problems accessing election-appeal mechanisms. Its roughly 60 percent figure is not used as a newly audited exact nationwide vote share. Accounts of specific arrest dates differ from the November Amnesty action, so the public dossier avoids a precise unified custody chronology. Allegations and detention are not criminal convictions. No original ballot audit or judicial determination about all election claims was reviewed.

sources.title: 1 September 2026: second-term oath, observer concerns and obstacles to election appeals
sources.findings: Read relevant Reuters sections from 1 September 2026. They corroborate the second-term oath and the 13 August election, report observer concerns and barriers to court access, and give the electoral commission’s response that courts should assess discrepancies. The article says observers still assessed that he would have won regardless of the cited irregularities; it does not report a judicial invalidation or establish that every criticism is proven. The profile records documented controversy without substituting it for legal findings. Financial-market performance in the article is not proof of democratic legitimacy or complete economic recovery.

sources.title: 17 November 2026 urgent action: concerns about detention and alleged mistreatment of 18 opposition members
sources.findings: Read Amnesty’s 17 November 2026 urgent-action document. It calls for release of 18 opposition members and alleges arbitrary detention, denial of legal/family access and mistreatment. These are the organisation’s allegations and advocacy, not a court conviction of Hichilema or proof he personally ordered every act. Its 14 August arrest description for Mundubile conflicts with AP’s account of hiding and surrender on 24 August; no exact merged timeline is asserted. The public text keeps the date and scope of Amnesty’s actual statement. Its request to send appeals is source content, not an instruction to contact anyone; no appeal was sent.

sources.title: November 2026 statement on the cabinet meeting held on 30 October during Hichilema’s second term
sources.findings: Read the Cabinet Office statement describing the third cabinet meeting of the second term, held on 30 October 2026. It says Hichilema called the meeting and confirms the ongoing administration. Calling a meeting is a documented governmental act, not independent proof of physical attendance. The introduction mentions the 2026 budget but the substantive section concerns proposed 2027 estimates; do not silently collapse those years. Cabinet approval of a proposed budget or approval to sign an agreement is not parliamentary enactment, expenditure execution, signature or entry into force. No claim is made that the planned 6 November budget presentation occurred solely from this prior statement.

sources.publisher: Government of Zambia, Ministry of Commerce, Trade and Industry
sources.title: Official text of the inaugural address delivered on 24 August 2021 in Lusaka
sources.findings: Read the cover and selected opening/policy passages of the government-hosted 24 August 2021 inaugural address. It explicitly gives the date, National Heroes Stadium in Lusaka and seventh-presidency identity, and states commitments on economic recovery, jobs, rights and rule of law. The February 2023 upload path is not the inauguration date. The speech attributes the UPND’s foundation to Mazoka and colleagues; Hichilema is its later leader. Written remarks were not checked against a recording word for word, and policy promises are not certified accomplishments.
